newsitem.title: UK: London gold slips lower still mulling Bundesbank.
newsitem.headline: London gold slips lower still mulling Bundesbank.

text.p: Precious metal market prices drifted lower on Thursday afternoon as participants continued to mull the overnight news that the German Ministry of Finance was considering revaluing its gold reserves.
A council meeting of the Bundesbank (German central bank) in which Finance Minister Theo Waigel participated cast no more light on the issue.
But dealers said the fact that Germany, hitherto the staunchest advocate of holding gold reserves as an anti-inflation safeguard, was talking about its bullion was scarey enough for the market.
"The market is right to sell this rumour," one senior dealer said and gold fixed at 1400 GMT at $346.40 per ounce against $348.10 this morning and a dollar higher on Wednesday afternoon.
The German government is under pressure to plug holes in its 1997 budget which was forecast to suffer a shortfall of between 18 billion and 20 billion marks.

Upgrading its 95 million ounces of gold reserves from the current 144 marks per ounce book value to closer to the market price of around 600 marks per ounce would release billions of marks in hidden reserves to help balance the budget.
The government is also looking at selling its share in recently privatised Deutsche Telekom.
"At the moment they cannot do either of these things. There have to be changes in the law," a gold dealer in Frankfurt said.

The overnight fall in gold prices -- first reports of the German thinking surfaced late in Wednesday's New York trading -- was mitigated by the weaker dollar against the yen which encouraged buying of gold in the Far East, dealers said.
However by mid afternoon the U.S. currency had bottomed against the yen and mark and another of gold's supportive influences was diminished.
After posting gains earlier, the highly volatile platinum and palladium (PGMs) markets both succumbed to profittaking in the afternoon encouraging cohort selling of gold.
"Gold is really marginalised. It's the PGMs which are capturing the attention," one dealer said.
The ultra-tight PGM markets have been forced higher by majpor exporter Russia failing to agree suply contracts with Japanese trading houses so far this year.
Platinum was down $2.30 at $393.25/$394.25 and palladium was off $2.00 at $173.00/$174.00.
